text:
jamie: quick idea dump 1: create a low-latency prefetch lane with its own small async queue + worker pool to isolate small-chat writes.

anya: makes sense. how do we classify requests into the lane?

jamie: heuristic: tokens<=8 OR client header x-latency=low. default heuristic covers most chat microbatches.

noel: fallback behaviour? if lane full do we sync-write?

jamie: prefer: try emergency shared pool, else return a soft-residency token and schedule fast background refetch. only sync if client requests strict_residency=true.

stef: watch fragmentation. many tiny staging allocations from lowlat lane could increase compaction frequency. add lane tags to allocations and tune compactor.

anya: metrics we need: lane_queue_depth, lane_sync_writes, soft_tokens_issued, prefetch_latency histogram.

jamie: rollout plan: feature-flagged on cluster, start on staging with lab tenants, then canary low-volume prod.

noel: ops: add a small unit test that simulates saturation and verifies soft-token vs sync when strict flag toggled.

ops-bot: deploy queued: jamie/prefetch-lane-proto -> staging in ~5m. :rocket:

stef: ok. jamie please post RFC link and basic perf numbers after staging run.
